citation: PCI Security Standards Council standard (contractual, not law)
summary: 12 requirement families for protecting cardholder data; enforced through card-brand and acquirer contracts.
applies_to: Any merchant or service provider that stores, processes or transmits payment card data.
size_thresholds: Validation level (SAQ vs. QSA ROC) depends on annual card-transaction volume under card-brand merchant-level programs. Those levels are set by the card brands and were not verified here.
status: v4.0.1 published June 11, 2024 (PCI SSC blog). Not a law. Check for any later revision.

summary: FTC treats unreasonable data security and misleading privacy claims as unfair or deceptive practices.
applies_to: For-profit businesses. Under 15 U.S.C. 44, 'corporation' covers only entities organized for their own or their members' profit, so most nonprofits fall outside FTC Section 5 jurisdiction.

summary: Any person that maintains or possesses consumer-report information for a business purpose must take reasonable measures when disposing of it.
applies_to: Employers, staffing firms and landlords that use background/consumer reports, plus their disposal vendors.

summary: Notify affected individuals (and often AGs) of breaches of personal information.
Written policy, retention schedule, informed written consent and restrictions on disclosure of biometric identifiers (e.g., fingerprint time clocks); private right of action.
applies_to: Private entities collecting biometrics from Illinois individuals (common for restaurant/hotel time clocks).
status: In force. The Illinois General Assembly site returned HTTP 503 and a certificate error (retried 2026-10-08), so the current text, including the 2024 amendment on per-person violations, was not verified

summary: Would require covered entities to report covered cyber incidents to CISA within 72 hours and ransom payments within 24 hours (proposed 226.5).
applies_to: Commercial Facilities Sector entities (lodging, food service) have no sector-specific criterion; only the size-based prong applies.
size_thresholds: Proposed 226.2(a): covered only if the entity exceeds the SBA small-business size standard for its NAICS code (13 CFR 121). Large hotel and restaurant chains could be covered.
status: PROPOSED ONLY. NPRM 89 FR 23644 (Apr 4, 2024). CISA held town halls (Feb 13 and May 26, 2026 notices) to refine scope. Fall 2025 Unified Agenda targeted a final rule for 09/2026. As of 2026-09-25 no final rule is in the Federal Register; CISA says it 'continues to work on the final rule.' Reporting is not yet mandatory.
